SK2008 A stored delegate captures a changing loop variable

A delegate added to a persistent List<TDelegate> captures a variable declared and incremented by an enclosing for loop.

CategoryCorrectness
Default severitywarning
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixno
Language version floor—
Since2.0

Why

Closures capture a variable rather than the value it had when the delegate was created. Delegates retained by the list can therefore all see the loop's final value instead of one value per iteration.

Example

Instead of:

for (var i = 0; i < 3; i++) { actions.Add(() => Use(i)); }

Write:

for (var i = 0; i < 3; i++) { var iteration = i; actions.Add(() => Use(iteration)); }

When it does not fire

The rule binds List<T>.Add and uses Roslyn capture analysis. It requires a delegate element type, a field receiver or a local declared outside the loop, and a control variable changed by built-in ++/-- or a nonzero constant integer +=/-= step. Other assignments and user-defined increment operators are not treated as proven changes. Per-iteration snapshots, foreach variables, nameof-only references, immediate invocations, custom Add methods and iteration-local lists are ignored. It does not infer arbitrary storage, mutation or invocation timing. A retained delegate intended to observe the final value needs an explicit suppression; no fix chooses or rewrites a captured identity.
